History:
- Main complaint: Decreased hearing in the left ear with numbness over the left jawline/around the left ear.
- Onset/duration: Approximately 3 weeks.
- Course: Persistent; numbness present most of the time, including during the visit.
- Associated symptoms: Intermittent ringing (tinnitus) in the left ear; occasional dizziness when tinnitus occurs.
- Pertinent negatives: No ear discharge, no ear pain, no ear itch, no fever. No weakness or numbness elsewhere. No difficulty swallowing or speaking. No vision problems.
- Impact: Limiting training/work as a jockey.

Past Medical History:
- Nasal polyps.
- Prior episode diagnosed “ages ago” as labyrinthitis (not ongoing).
- Allergies: Latex.
- Medications:
  - Nasal spray for nasal polyps (name/dose/route/frequency not documented; used as needed; originally prescribed).
  - Rennie’s antacid (dose/route/frequency not documented; used as needed).
- Family history: Brother with neurofibromatosis.
- Social: Works as a jockey. Living situation conflict (see Quality checks).

Physical Examination:
- Video visit only; no in-person physical exam performed.
- No vitals documented.
- Plan made for in-person neurologic exam and otoscopic ear exam today.

Impression:
- Unilateral left-sided hearing decrease with persistent left facial numbness and intermittent tinnitus/dizziness; clinician considering possible Bell’s palsy but in-person neurologic and ear examination needed to confirm and exclude other causes.

Management Plan:
- Same-day, face-to-face clinic appointment arranged for full neurologic examination and otoscopic evaluation.
- Reassurance provided: Condition not thought to be life-threatening based on history, but needs in-person assessment to confirm.
- Administrative plan: Patient to call support team after 5 minutes to schedule a same-day slot at a convenient Central London clinic (number to be placed in notes).
- No medications started; no tests ordered during this video visit.

Patient Summary:
- A 40-year-old with 3 weeks of left-sided hearing loss and left facial numbness, plus intermittent tinnitus and brief dizziness. No red flag neurologic deficits reported. The clinician suspects possible Bell’s palsy but requires same-day in-person neurologic and otoscopic examination to confirm and further reassure.

Key Takeaways:
- Attend the same-day in-person clinic appointment today for a neurologic and ear exam.
- Based on current information, this does not appear life-threatening, but confirmation requires examination.
- Call the support team shortly to secure today’s appointment slot as instructed.

Next Steps:
- Same-day in-person evaluation: comprehensive neurologic exam and inspection of the left ear (otoscopy).
- Further management to be guided by findings at the in-person visit.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: No vitals; no comprehensive medication reconciliation (names/doses/frequencies/routes unclear for nasal spray and Rennie’s); no past surgeries; no tobacco/alcohol/drug history; no immunization status; no detailed neurologic exam findings; no baseline audiology or hearing test.
- Internal conflicts: Living situation—patient initially agreed to “live alone” then stated living with a partner (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: Several pauses/inaudible or incomplete segments; some details (e.g., exact medication name) unclear.
